name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi
description: Central Sector Scheme providing income support of Rs. 6,000 per year to all landholding farmer families across the country, paid in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000 every four months directly into Aadhaar-linked bank accounts via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
benefits: Rs. 6,000 per year in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000
Direct Benefit Transfer to Aadhaar-linked bank accounts
No intermediary — funds transferred directly by Government of India
eligibility: All landholding farmer families with cultivable land
Must be an Indian citizen
Must have Aadhaar-linked bank account
eKYC completion is mandatory
Institutional landholders are excluded
Income tax payers are excluded
Serving or retired government officers (above MTS/Group D) are excluded
Professionals registered with professional bodies (doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs, architects) are excluded
Pensioners receiving monthly pension of Rs. 10,000 or more are excluded
applicationProcess: Visit the official PM-KISAN portal at https://pmkisan.gov.in
Click on 'New Farmer Registration' under Farmer's Corner
Select Rural or Urban farmer registration
Enter Aadhaar number and fill required details
Application verified by state/district authorities
Alternatively, visit nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) for registration
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
description: Government-sponsored crop insurance scheme that provides comprehensive insurance coverage against crop loss due to non-preventable natural risks including drought, flood, cyclone, hailstorm, pest/disease attacks, and other natural calamities. It integrates multiple stakeholders on a single platform.
benefits: Comprehensive crop insurance against natural calamities, pests, and diseases
Low premium rates: 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, 5% for commercial/horticultural crops
Balance premium paid by Government (Centre and State in 50:50 ratio)
Coverage from pre-sowing to post-harvest (up to 14 days)
Individual farm-level loss assessment using technology (satellite imagery, drones, smartphones)
eligibility: All farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing notified crops in notified areas
Loanee farmers covered on a voluntary basis (since Kharif 2020)
Non-loanee farmers can voluntarily opt for the scheme
Enrollment within the cut-off dates notified for each season
requiredDocuments: Land ownership records / tenancy agreement / lease agreement
Crop sowing certificate from village revenue officer
applicationProcess: Visit the official PMFBY portal at https://pmfby.gov.in
Register as a farmer user
Select the season, year, state, district, and crop
Fill in bank details and land information
Pay the farmer's share of premium
Alternatively, apply through nearest bank branch or CSC
For grievances, use Krishi Rakshak Portal or call helpline 14447
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme
description: Government-sponsored crop insurance scheme that uses weather parameters (rainfall, temperature, relative humidity, wind speed) as a proxy for crop yields to provide financial protection to farmers against weather-related crop losses. Claims are settled based on data from Automatic Weather Stations.
benefits: Financial protection against weather-related crop losses (drought, excess rain, extreme temperatures, humidity, wind)
Faster claim settlement based on objective weather data from Automatic Weather Stations
Subsidized premium rates similar to PMFBY
Transparent process with no manual yield estimation disputes
eligibility: All farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing notified crops in notified areas
Loanee farmers who have availed seasonal agricultural operation loans for notified crops
Non-loanee farmers who voluntarily opt for coverage
requiredDocuments: Land ownership records or tenancy/lease agreement
applicationProcess: Visit the official PMFBY portal at https://pmfby.gov.in
Register as a farmer user
Select RWBCIS and fill in required details
Alternatively, apply through nearest bank branch or CSC
For grievances, use Krishi Rakshak Portal or call helpline 14447
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana
description: Voluntary and contributory pension scheme for Small and Marginal Farmers (SMF) that provides a minimum monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 after attaining the age of 60. The Government of India provides an equal matching contribution to the pension fund managed by LIC.
benefits: Minimum monthly pension of Rs. 3,000 after age 60
Government provides equal matching contribution
Family pension: Spouse receives 50% of pension on farmer's death
Monthly contribution ranges from Rs. 55 to Rs. 200 depending on age of entry
Option to have contribution debited from PM-KISAN benefits
eligibility: Small and Marginal Farmers owning cultivable land up to 2 hectares
Age between 18 and 40 years
Must not be covered under other social security schemes (NPS, EPFO, etc.)
Must not hold constitutional or high-ranking government posts
requiredDocuments: Bank account or savings bank passbook
Land ownership records as per state land records
applicationProcess: Visit the official portal at https://maandhan.in
Register online with Aadhaar and bank details
Alternatively, visit nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) for free enrollment
PM-KISAN beneficiaries can opt for auto-debit from PM-KISAN installments
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Kisan Credit Card Scheme
description: Government-backed credit scheme providing timely and adequate short-term credit to farmers for crop production, post-harvest expenses, consumption needs, and working capital for allied activities including animal husbandry and fisheries, at concessional interest rates.
benefits: Short-term credit at 7% per annum interest rate
Effective interest rate as low as 4% per annum with 2% interest subvention and 3% prompt repayment incentive
Revolving cash credit facility — withdraw as needed
ATM-enabled RuPay debit card
Crop insurance under PMFBY included
Personal accident insurance coverage
Collateral-free loans up to Rs. 2 lakh
Card valid for 5 years with annual review
10% annual increment for cost escalation
eligibility: Owner cultivators (individual or joint)
Tenant farmers, oral lessees, and sharecroppers
Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers
Farmers engaged in crop production, animal husbandry, or fisheries
requiredDocuments: Completed application form (simplified one-page form available)
Proof of landholding certified by revenue authorities
applicationProcess: Visit nearest bank branch (scheduled commercial bank, cooperative bank, RRB)
Submit completed KCC application form with required documents
PM-KISAN beneficiaries can apply through PM-KISAN portal
Apply through Common Service Centre (CSC)
Check eligibility through Jan Samarth portal (https://www.jansamarth.in)
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare / Reserve Bank of India / NABARD

name: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana - Per Drop More Crop
description: Central government scheme promoting micro-irrigation (drip and sprinkler systems) to improve water use efficiency in agriculture under the 'Per Drop More Crop' component. Provides subsidies to farmers for adoption of precision irrigation technologies.
benefits: 55% subsidy on micro-irrigation equipment for Small and Marginal Farmers
45% subsidy on micro-irrigation equipment for other farmers
Support for drip irrigation, sprinkler irrigation, and other precision irrigation systems
Improved water use efficiency and crop productivity
Funding shared between Centre and State (60:40 ratio for general states)
eligibility: All categories of farmers (small, marginal, medium, large) owning agricultural land
Members of cooperatives, SHGs, incorporated companies, and water user associations
Contract or lease farmers with lease agreement for minimum 7 years
Financial assistance limited to maximum 5 hectares per beneficiary
Repeat assistance eligible only after projected life of system (7 years)
requiredDocuments: Proof of land ownership (ROR / Land records / Patta)
Caste certificate (if applicable for specific state subsidies)
applicationProcess: Apply through State Agriculture Department — visit nearest Block Agriculture Office
Check state-specific online portals for registration
Submit application with required documents
Verification and approval by district/state authorities
Subsidy disbursed via DBT after installation and verification
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization
description: Central government scheme to promote agricultural mechanization by providing subsidies for purchase of farm machinery and equipment. The scheme aims to increase farm productivity by making modern agricultural equipment affordable for farmers through financial assistance.
benefits: 50% subsidy for Small and Marginal Farmers, SC/ST farmers, women farmers, and NE/Himalayan state farmers
40% subsidy for other categories of farmers
Higher subsidies (80-100%) for establishing Custom Hiring Centres and Farm Machinery Banks
Subsidy via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) after purchase verification
Covers wide range of equipment: tractors, tillers, harvesters, sprayers, seed drills, etc.
eligibility: All farmers with valid land ownership or lease documents
Priority for small and marginal farmers
SC/ST farmers and women farmers eligible for higher subsidies
Equipment must be purchased from authorized manufacturer/dealer on DBT portal
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card or valid identity proof
applicationProcess: Visit the official portal at https://agrimachinery.nic.in
Register as a farmer and fill personal, land, and bank details
Select desired machinery and submit application
Keep Application ID for tracking status
Selection may be through online lottery if applications exceed target
After approval, purchase equipment from authorized dealer
Subsidy credited via DBT after verification
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Soil Health Card Scheme
description: Government of India scheme that provides soil health cards to farmers with crop-specific recommendations on nutrients and fertilizers. The card contains detailed analysis of 12 essential soil parameters to help farmers optimize fertilizer use, reduce costs, and improve crop productivity.
benefits: Detailed report on 12 soil parameters: N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC, and Organic Carbon
Crop-specific fertilizer and soil amendment recommendations
Helps prevent overuse of chemicals and fertilizers
Reduces farming costs through optimized nutrient management
Cards available in multiple languages for download on official portal
Free of cost to all farmers
eligibility: All farmers across India — no restrictive eligibility criteria
Scheme aims to cover all land holdings for sustainable agriculture
applicationProcess: State government officials collect soil samples from farmers' fields (15-20 cm depth) using GPS-based tools
Samples tested at authorized Soil Testing Laboratories
Results updated on the official SHC portal and Soil Health Card generated
Farmers can search and download their card at https://soilhealth.dac.gov.in using phone number or name
SMS notification sent to farmers when card is ready
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana
description: Sub-component of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) promoting organic farming through cluster-based approaches. Provides financial assistance to farmers for adopting organic farming practices using traditional, eco-friendly, and low-cost technologies with Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India) certification.
benefits: Financial assistance of approximately Rs. 31,000 to Rs. 50,000 per hectare over 3 years
Support for organic inputs, on-farm input infrastructure, and marketing
Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India) organic certification
Cluster-based approach (20 hectares) for shared resources and collective marketing
Funding: 60:40 (Centre:State) for general states; 90:10 for NE/Himalayan states
eligibility: All farmers and institutions interested in transitioning to organic farming
Must be willing to join a cluster or Local Group
Must adopt organic practices compliant with PGS-India standards
Focus on smallholder farmers
applicationProcess: Contact local Department of Agriculture or regional councils/nodal agencies
Register through state-specific agricultural portals
Join an existing cluster or form a new Local Group
Visit the Jaivik Kheti Portal (https://jaivikkheti.in) for registration and guidelines
Contact district agriculture office for current application procedures
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan
description: Flagship scheme of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) promoting solar energy in agriculture through three components: ground-mounted solar power plants, standalone solar agriculture pumps, and solarization of existing grid-connected agriculture pumps.
benefits: Component A: Decentralized ground-mounted solar/RE power plants (500 kW to 2 MW) on barren/fallow land
Component B: Standalone solar agriculture pumps for individual farmers in off-grid areas
Component C: Solarization of existing grid-connected agriculture pumps
Central subsidy of approximately 30% and state subsidy of approximately 30% (farmer contributes remaining 40%)
Reliable daytime power for irrigation, reducing dependence on diesel
Additional income from selling surplus solar power to the grid
eligibility: Individual farmers, groups of farmers, cooperatives, panchayats, FPOs, and Water User Associations
For Component A: Farmers with barren, fallow, or agricultural land
For Component B: Farmers in off-grid areas needing irrigation
For Component C: Farmers with existing grid-connected agriculture pumps
requiredDocuments: Proof of land ownership or valid lease agreement
Existing electricity connection details (for pump-related components)
applicationProcess: Visit the official PM-KUSUM portal at https://pmkusum.mnre.gov.in
Select your state to see local registration options
Apply through your respective state's agriculture/renewable energy department portal
Alternatively, visit nearest Agriculture Department or state nodal agency office
WARNING: Do not use unofficial websites or apps — official registration is free through government channels
source: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India

name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund
description: Central Sector Scheme providing medium-to-long-term debt financing for investment in viable post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets. Offers interest subvention and credit guarantee coverage on loans from participating financial institutions.
benefits: 3% per annum interest subvention on loans up to Rs. 2 crore per project for 7 years
Credit guarantee coverage under CGTMSE for loans up to Rs. 2 crore (government pays the fee)
Convergence with other Central and State schemes (PMFME, SMAM, PM-KUSUM, MIDH, etc.)
Supports warehouses, cold storage, silos, sorting/grading/packaging units, logistics facilities
Supports precision agriculture, farm automation, drones, IoT, AI applications
eligibility: Individual farmers (subject to guidelines)
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Cooperatives, SHGs, JLGs
Agri-entrepreneurs and startups
Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs)
Custom Hiring Centre (CHC) owners and agri-service providers
State agencies, local bodies, and PPP projects
requiredDocuments: Land ownership or lease documents for the project site
applicationProcess: Visit the official AIF portal at https://agriinfra.dac.gov.in
Register and submit a project proposal
Loan sanctioned by participating financial institution (commercial banks, cooperative banks, RRBs, SFBs, NBFCs)
Interest subvention and credit guarantee automatically applied on eligible loans
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: National Agriculture Market
description: Pan-India electronic trading portal that networks existing APMC mandis into a unified national market for agricultural commodities. Promotes transparency, better price discovery, and efficient marketing by enabling online bidding and direct electronic payments to farmers.
benefits: Transparent online bidding for better price discovery
Access to buyers and traders beyond local mandis — national marketplace
Digital recording of arrivals, quality assaying, and auctioning for fair transactions
Direct electronic payments (RTGS, NEFT, BHIM, UPI) to farmer's bank account
Real-time market prices and trade information via e-NAM mobile app
Free registration for farmers
eligibility: Any farmer with agricultural land in a state/UT connected to the e-NAM network
Registration on e-NAM portal is free
requiredDocuments: Personal details (Name, Address, DOB, Mobile Number)
Bank account details (passbook or cheque leaf)
applicationProcess: Visit the official portal at https://www.enam.gov.in
Select 'Registration' as 'Farmer' and fill in required details
Alternatively, visit nearest e-NAM enabled mandi with documents
Details verified by selected APMC
Receive login ID and password after approval
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture
description: Centrally sponsored scheme for holistic growth of the horticulture sector covering fruits, vegetables, root and tuber crops, mushrooms, spices, flowers, aromatic plants, coconut, cashew, cocoa, and bamboo. Provides financial and technical support through multiple sub-missions including NHM, HMNEH, NHB, and CDB.
benefits: Approximately 50% subsidy for protected cultivation (polyhouses, greenhouses above 500 sqm)
45-55% subsidy for micro-irrigation, with higher support for small and marginal farmers
35-50% financial assistance for cold chain and post-harvest management infrastructure
Assistance for nurseries and tissue culture units for quality planting material
Funding: 60:40 (Centre:State) for general states; 90:10 for NE/Himalayan states
eligibility: Farmers engaged in horticulture
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs)
Farmer Interest Groups (FIGs)
Other eligible horticulture stakeholders
applicationProcess: Contact District Horticulture Officer or nearest State Horticulture Mission office
Submit application through state-specific agricultural portals
Use MIDH Suraksha mobile app to track applications and inspections
Verification and approval by state horticulture department
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations
description: Central Sector Scheme to organize farmers into Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) for achieving economies of scale in production, marketing, and value addition. Provides holistic support including financial assistance, matching equity grants, credit guarantee, and professional handholding for 5 years.
benefits: Management and handholding cost: up to Rs. 18 lakh per FPO over 3 years
Matching equity grant: up to Rs. 2,000 per farmer member, maximum Rs. 15 lakh per FPO
Credit guarantee cover for project loans up to Rs. 2 crore per FPO
Professional support by Cluster-Based Business Organization (CBBO) for 5 years
Assistance with business planning, registration, market linkages, and capacity building
eligibility: Small, marginal, and landless farmers
Farmers in agricultural and horticultural production
Minimum 300 farmer-members required (100 in NE and hilly areas)
Must be registered under Part IXA of Companies Act, 2013 (Producer Company) or State Cooperative Societies Act
requiredDocuments: List of farmer members with identity details
Bank account details of the FPO
applicationProcess: Form a group of eligible farmers meeting minimum membership requirements
Register as Producer Company or Cooperative Society
Apply through implementing agencies: SFAC, NABARD, or NCDC
Visit SFAC portal at https://sfacindia.com for detailed guidelines
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm
description: Centrally sponsored scheme to increase oil palm cultivation and reduce India's dependence on edible oil imports. Provides subsidies for planting materials, drip irrigation, farm machinery, maintenance, intercropping incentives, and includes a Viability Gap Payment mechanism to protect farmers from international price fluctuations.
benefits: Subsidies for high-quality oil palm seedlings
Assistance for drip irrigation, farm machinery, and harvesting tools
Support for plantation maintenance during gestation period
Incentives for intercropping during first 4 years before full production
Viability Gap Payment (VGP) to protect farmers from international CPO price fluctuations
Development of oil palm processing infrastructure
eligibility: Farmers interested in oil palm cultivation in identified districts of participating states
Must have suitable land for oil palm cultivation
Priority given to small and marginal farmers
requiredDocuments: Aadhaar Card and Aadhaar-linked mobile number
Land ownership documents or land records
Bank account details (for DBT of subsidies)
Soil test report or water source proof (if requested by department)
applicationProcess: Contact local District Agriculture Officer or Horticulture Department office
Register through state-specific agricultural portals
Submit application with required documents
Visit nearest Uzhavar Maiyam (Farmers' Centre) in Tamil Nadu for assistance
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Namo Drone Didi
description: Central Sector Scheme to provide drones to 15,000 Women Self-Help Groups (SHGs) under DAY-NRLM for offering agricultural drone rental services to farmers. Provides 80% subsidy on drone cost, training for drone pilots, and supports income generation for women SHGs.
benefits: 80% Central Financial Assistance on drone cost, up to Rs. 8 lakh
Remaining cost covered through AIF loan with 3% interest subvention
Mandatory training: one SHG member as drone pilot, one as drone assistant
Income generation for women SHGs through drone rental services
Precision application of fertilizers and pesticides for farmers
eligibility: Women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) promoted under DAY-NRLM
SHGs must be part of identified clusters for drone usage
requiredDocuments: Bank account details of the SHG
applicationProcess: Apply through DAY-NRLM channels at state/district level
Selection of SHGs by implementing agencies
Training provided to selected SHG members
Drone provided after successful completion of training
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare / Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India

name: Digital Agriculture Mission
description: Umbrella scheme to build Digital Public Infrastructure for agriculture including AgriStack (Farmer Registry, Geo-Referenced Village Maps, Crop Sown Registry), Krishi Decision Support System (KDSS), and Soil Resource Mapping at village level. Creates a farmer-centric digital identity system for improving access to credit, insurance, and government services.
benefits: Unique Farmer ID (Kisan ki Pehchaan) for easier access to credit, insurance, and procurement
Farmers' Registry linking demographics and land holdings digitally
Crop Sown Registry for tracking what farmers grow
Satellite-based crop mapping and automated yield estimation
Village-level soil resource mapping using high-resolution data
Evidence-based decision support for farmers and government
eligibility: All farmers across India benefit through creation of Farmer IDs
Government-led initiative — no direct application required from farmers
applicationProcess: Government-led initiative implemented by Central and State Governments
Farmer IDs being created through coordination with state agriculture departments
No separate application process for farmers — integration with existing schemes
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

name: Kalaignarin All Village Integrated Agricultural Development Programme
description: Major initiative of the Government of Tamil Nadu for comprehensive agricultural development across all 12,525 village panchayats over 5 years. Integrates services from over 15 government departments to fulfill farmers' needs, increase income, bring fallow lands under cultivation, and promote sustainable rural development.
benefits: Sinking of borewells in fallow land clusters
Establishment of farm ponds
Desilting of channels, tanks, and ooranis (traditional water bodies)
100% subsidy for Adi Dravida farmers for wells, drip irrigation, and farm ponds
Distribution of coconut, horticultural, and tree saplings
Home garden and vegetable cultivation kits with Rs. 5,000 incentive
Distribution of farming sprayers and pulse seeds for bund cropping
Subsidies for agricultural machinery
Formation of Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) with technical training
Increased access to crop loans through cooperative societies
eligibility: Farming families residing in selected village panchayats in Tamil Nadu
All districts except Chennai and Nilgiris
Specific components may have additional criteria based on land ownership, social category, or small/marginal farmer status
Special provisions for Adi Dravida (SC/ST) farmers
applicationProcess: Contact local Agriculture Department office
Visit Village Panchayat office for information on active components
Contact district Agricultural Engineering Department
Apply through local Assistant Agricultural Officer (AAO)
Visit TNAU Agritech Portal (https://agritech.tnau.ac.in) for technical guidance
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu

name: Tamil Nadu Millet Mission
description: State-led mission focused on increasing area, production, and productivity of millets (Pearl Millet/Cumbu, Sorghum/Cholam, Finger Millet/Ragi) in Tamil Nadu. Supports approximately 4.75 lakh farmers across 11.80 lakh acres with subsidies, seed minikits, machinery hiring centres, and processing centres.
benefits: Subsidies through alternate crop cultivation packages
Distribution of seed minikits for improved millet varieties
Establishment of Agricultural Machinery Hiring Centres
Establishment of Primary Processing Centres
Training on modern cultivation technologies and value addition
Formation of farmer groups for collective marketing
Outlay of Rs. 63.81 crore jointly funded by Union and State governments
eligibility: Farmers residing in Tamil Nadu
Farmers engaged in cultivation of major or minor millets
Farmers looking to adopt improved millet cultivation technologies
applicationProcess: Contact nearest Assistant Agricultural Officer (AAO) at village level
Visit Agricultural Officer (AO) at Block level for current application procedures
Enrollment notifications issued through official state agricultural portals or local block offices
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu

name: Tamil Nadu Minor Millet Mission
description: State-funded mission to promote minor millets including foxtail millet, little millet, kodo millet, barnyard millet, and proso millet in Tamil Nadu. Allocated Rs. 7.61 crore from state funds to support farmers in cultivating and marketing minor millets.
benefits: Subsidies for minor millet cultivation
Distribution of improved seed varieties
Support for value addition and processing
Marketing support for minor millet products
eligibility: Farmers residing in Tamil Nadu
Farmers engaged in or interested in minor millet cultivation
applicationProcess: Contact nearest Assistant Agricultural Officer (AAO)
Visit Agricultural Officer (AO) at Block level
Apply through local agriculture department office
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu

name: Chief Minister's Uzhavar Pathukappu Thittam
description: Social security and welfare scheme of the Government of Tamil Nadu for farmers and agricultural labourers. Provides financial assistance for marriage, educational expenses, old-age pensions, accident relief, and funeral expenses. Also includes input subsidies for seeds, bio-fertilizers, and irrigation.
benefits: Financial assistance for marriage expenses
Support for educational expenses of farmer families
Old-age pension for farmers
Accident relief and disability compensation
Funeral expense assistance
Input subsidies for seeds and bio-fertilizers
Support for drip/sprinkler irrigation adoption
eligibility: Small and marginal farmers in Tamil Nadu
Farmers engaged in horticulture, sericulture, dairy farming, poultry, and inland fishing
Agricultural labourers
Farmers who utilize regulated markets for their produce
applicationProcess: Apply through local Agriculture Extension Officer
Visit nearest Block Agricultural Office
Submit application with required documents
Check official state portal at https://agri.tn.gov.in for updates
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu

name: Tamil Nadu Micro Irrigation Scheme
description: Tamil Nadu state scheme providing high subsidies for micro-irrigation systems (drip and sprinkler) to farmers under the PMKSY framework. Small and marginal farmers receive up to 100% subsidy and other farmers up to 75% subsidy for drip and sprinkler irrigation installation.
benefits: Up to 100% subsidy for Small and Marginal Farmers for drip and sprinkler irrigation
Up to 75% subsidy for other farmers
Coverage up to 5 hectares per beneficiary
Improved water use efficiency and crop productivity
Installation by empanelled micro-irrigation companies
eligibility: Must be a farmer cultivating land in Tamil Nadu
Maximum coverage of 5 hectares per beneficiary
Must have a water source (well, borewell, or canal)
Land ownership documents required
requiredDocuments: Land records (proof of ownership - Patta, Chitta, Adangal)
Bank account details (for Direct Benefit Transfer)
Proof of water source (well, borewell, or canal)
applicationProcess: Apply through Tamil Nadu Horticulture Development Agency
Apply through Uzhavan App
Officials from Agricultural Engineering Department conduct site inspection
Technical sanction issued after inspection
System installed by empanelled micro-irrigation company
Subsidy disbursed after final verification of installation
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare / Agricultural Engineering Department, Government of Tamil Nadu

name: Tamil Nadu Seed Multiplication Scheme
description: Tamil Nadu state scheme providing subsidies and premium payments to farmers who produce seeds (paddy, millets, pulses, oilseeds, cotton) under contract with the Department of Agriculture. Ensures availability of quality certified seeds for the state's agricultural needs.
benefits: Subsidies for seed production under contract farming
Premium payments over market price for quality seed production
Support for certified seed production of paddy, millets, pulses, oilseeds, and cotton
Technical guidance from Department of Agriculture
eligibility: Farmers in Tamil Nadu willing to produce seeds under contract with the Department of Agriculture
Must follow quality standards and guidelines prescribed by the department
applicationProcess: Collect application form from nearest Agricultural Office
Fill out the form and attach mandatory documents
Submit application to Assistant Agricultural Officer at village level or Agricultural/Deputy Agricultural Officer at block level
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu / myScheme.gov.in

name: Distribution of Certified Seeds of Maize - Tamil Nadu
description: Tamil Nadu state scheme providing subsidized certified maize seeds to farmers in select districts including Coimbatore, Erode, Salem, Madurai, and others to improve maize productivity and adoption of improved varieties.
benefits: Subsidized certified maize seeds for farmers
Improved maize varieties for better productivity
Focus on select maize-growing districts
eligibility: Maize-growing farmers in selected districts of Tamil Nadu (Coimbatore, Erode, Salem, Madurai, etc.)
Must be a farmer residing in Tamil Nadu
applicationProcess: Collect application form from nearest Agricultural Office
Fill out form and attach mandatory documents
Submit to Assistant Agricultural Officer or Agricultural Officer at block level
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu / myScheme.gov.in

name: Distribution of Minikits (Maize) - Tamil Nadu
description: Tamil Nadu state scheme providing free-of-cost minikits to maize-growing farmers in select districts to promote adoption of improved maize varieties and demonstrate modern cultivation practices.
benefits: Free-of-cost maize minikits to farmers
Improved hybrid/variety seeds for demonstration
Technical guidance on maize cultivation
eligibility: Maize-growing farmers in selected districts of Tamil Nadu
Priority for small, marginal, SC/ST, and women farmers
applicationProcess: Contact nearest Agricultural Office for availability
Submit application to Assistant Agricultural Officer at village level
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu / myScheme.gov.in

name: Block Demonstrations for Pulses - Tamil Nadu
description: Tamil Nadu state scheme organizing block-level demonstrations for pulse crops to showcase improved technologies and varieties. Provides subsidy of 50% of input costs or Rs. 2,000 per demonstration to participating farmers.
benefits: Subsidy of 50% of input costs or Rs. 2,000 per demonstration
Exposure to improved pulse cultivation technologies
Free inputs for demonstration plots
eligibility: Farmers in Tamil Nadu willing to participate in pulse crop demonstrations
Priority for small, marginal, SC/ST, and women farmers
applicationProcess: Contact nearest Agricultural Office
Apply through Assistant Agricultural Officer at village level or Agricultural Officer at block level
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu / myScheme.gov.in

name: Block Demonstrations for Maize - Tamil Nadu
description: Tamil Nadu state scheme organizing block demonstrations for maize cultivation. Provides Rs. 4,000 per demonstration for 1-hectare plots to showcase modern maize cultivation techniques, with special focus on small, marginal, SC/ST, and women farmers.
benefits: Rs. 4,000 per demonstration for 1-hectare plots
Exposure to modern maize cultivation techniques
Free inputs and technical guidance for demonstration
eligibility: Farmers in Tamil Nadu willing to participate in maize demonstrations
Special focus on small, marginal, SC/ST, and women farmers
applicationProcess: Collect application form from nearest Agricultural Office
Fill form and attach documents including proof of identity and land ownership
Submit to Assistant Agricultural Officer (village level) or Agricultural/Deputy Agricultural Officer (block level)
source: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu / myScheme.gov.in

name: Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank Loan (Horticulture) - Tamil Nadu
description: Tamil Nadu scheme providing loans ranging from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 2,00,000 per 0.4 hectare through Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks to support horticultural activities in the state.
benefits: Loans from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 2,00,000 per 0.4 hectare
Support for horticultural crop cultivation
Cooperative bank lending with favorable terms
